description: Fluctuations in anthropogenic nighttime lights from satellite imagery for five cities in Niger and Nigeria is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Nita Bharti et al. Dynamic measures of human populations can inform global health management but are often overlooked, largely because they are difficult to quantify. Measuring human population dynamics can be prohibitively expensive in under-resourced communities. Satellite imagery can provide measurements of human populations, past and present, to complement public health analyses and interventions. Coverage: global (NG); published in 2018. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in scholarsphere and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
